top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is the one candidate whose concept is new in kind: event-driven pharmacology in which a designed molecule brings an E3 ligase and a target together so the target is removed. Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated it in 2001, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained a whole drug class and showed the same logic works through glues, with VHL and cereblon mechanisms confirmed independently in many laboratories. The citation can span both strands under the ubiquitin-proteasome system. I rank the Ciulli variant (P002) next because it is the same field and I would not oppose it, then the clean Buchwald-Hartwig pair (P001) as the safest well-attributed, fully mature alternative, ahead of lipid nanoparticles (credit spread, mRNA headline recognised in 2023) and sequencing by synthesis (category and prior-prize concerns). No award is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, but no proposal involves her work or a conflict for me
